summary: The article accurately explains the new UPI interchange fee rules, their effective date, and their impact on various transaction types, including exemptions for recurring payments. It correctly identifies who bears the fee and clarifies that consumers are generally not directly charged.

claims.claim: New UPI rules effective October 15 introduce an interchange fee of 0.4% for merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the effective date of October 15, 2026, and the 0.4% interchange fee for merchant transactions exceeding ₹2,000.

claims.claim: This fee is primarily levied on Payment System Providers (PSPs) and the acquiring bank, not directly on consumers for most transactions.
claims.note: Sources clarify that the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is borne by merchants and shared within the payment ecosystem, with banks advised not to pass it on to customers. UPI application providers are also prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges on customers.

claims.claim: Person-to-person (P2P) UPI transfers, which constitute a significant portion of UPI usage, will continue to remain free.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions remain free, irrespective of the amount.

claims.claim: Recurring payments set up via UPI AutoPay for services like insurance premiums, SIPs, and subscription bills are exempt from this new interchange fee.
claims.note: Sources explicitly state that automated recurring payments through UPI mandates or AutoPay, including for utility bills, OTT subscriptions, and recurring investments, do not attract the prescribed MDR transaction charge.

claims.claim: For specified merchant categories such as railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, UPI transactions above ₹2,000 will attract a flat ₹5 MDR per transaction, rather than the regular 0.4% structure.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the flat ₹5 MDR for specific categories like railways, telecom, insurance, and fuel for transactions above ₹2,000.

claims.claim: For transactions of ₹75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at ₹300 per transaction.
claims.note: Sources confirm the cap of ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above.

claims.claim: UPI currently doesn't support recurring transactions of greater than 15,000 INR in value.
claims.note: Stripe documentation and other sources indicate that UPI AutoPay has a limit of ₹15,000 for recurring transactions without additional authentication. Transactions exceeding this amount require AFA each time.

article_title: Understanding New UPI Rules: Impact on Insurance, SIPs, and AutoPay
